statement_source_and_scope_match: Baigent B, Theorem 1 AS1–AS4 gives the precise C1 map class; §6 asks about unresolved interior regularity. MNR §1 independently reports the unknown nonconvex case and lack of known interior nonsmooth examples. The question fixes C1 interior regularity, not the known conditional boundary-neat-embedding characterization. Radial and embedded formulations agree since an unordered C1 interior hypersurface has a nonnegative normal and every radial vector there is strictly positive, hence transverse.
proposed_statement_text:
For an integer $d\ge3$, set $C=[0,\infty)^d$ and consider the population map $F_i(x)=x_i f_i(x)$. Suppose $f$ is $C^1$ on an open neighborhood of $C$, $f_i(x)>0$ and $\partial f_i/\partial x_j(x)<0$ on $C$ for all $i,j$. Each positive coordinate axis has a fixed point $q_i e_i$, with $q_i>0$. For $q=(q_1,\ldots,q_d)$ assume

$$
\rho(M(x))<1\quad(x\in[0,q]),\qquad
M_{ij}(x)=-\frac{x_i}{f_i(x)}\frac{\partial f_i}{\partial x_j}(x),
$$

where $\rho$ denotes spectral radius and $[0,q]=\prod_i[0,q_i]$. These hypotheses guarantee a carrying simplex $\Sigma\subset C\setminus\{0\}$: a compact invariant unordered hypersurface to whose trajectories every nonzero trajectory is asymptotic. Here unordered means that no two distinct points are comparable coordinatewise.

Is $\Sigma\cap(0,\infty)^d$ necessarily a $C^1$ embedded $(d-1)$-dimensional submanifold for every such map? Equivalently, write $\Sigma=\{R(u)u:u\in\Delta\}$, where $\Delta=\{u\in C:\sum_i u_i=1\}$ and $R:\Delta\to(0,\infty)$ is its continuous radial representation: must $R$ be $C^1$ on the relative interior of $\Delta$? Only interior regularity is requested; no smoothness or transverse embedding at extinction faces is assumed.
applied_significance: Competition maps describe populations whose per-capita growth decreases with every population density. Their carrying simplex contains the long-term nonzero dynamics. Interior C1 regularity would justify smooth geometric reduction when analyzing coexistence, invariant manifolds and changes of stability.

hypothesis_comparison: BEN works with a diffeomorphism to its image defined on all of R^m, with a strictly positive derivative everywhere. The inverse of the candidate map has the needed positivity locally in the positive orthant; a global extension retaining these hypotheses has not been established.

The stated higher-regularity results concern a basin of a compact attractor within a nonmonotone manifold and impose differentiability/gap conditions. Neither such an interior compact core for inverse dynamics nor those extra conditions is part of the candidate.

M99 §1 explicitly applies Tereščák only to the repulsion basin of a repeller contained in the positive orthant. The whole carrying simplex meets coordinate faces where the strong positivity fails; the candidate does not assume all backward interior orbits remain away from those faces.
CONVEX §1 and MNR §1 continue to identify the interior problem as open after these monotone-dynamics results.
later_results_and_resolution_checks.scope_relation: No matching direct or indirect resolution identified; a local inverse-positivity observation is insufficient to import the global theorem.
later_results_and_resolution_checks.assessment_and_remaining_gap: The inspected conditional basin results leave arbitrary interior points in the stated class unresolved. The original Tereščák theorem is not claimed to have been read.

closest_existing_or_new_entries.difference: Existence of a finite-dimensional Lipschitz inertial manifold for an infinite-dimensional Navier–Stokes PDE; candidate concerns C1 regularity of an already existing finite-dimensional population hypersurface.
Competitive exclusion for a spatial stochastic particle model, not discrete deterministic geometric regularity.
Persistence of bounded weakly reversible mass-action ODEs; neither map model nor regularity target agrees.
Global attraction for a scalar delay equation under local stability, not carrying-simplex differentiability.

duplicate_review.distinctness_reason: No baseline, accepted or held candidate has this model and interior-geometric target. Broad biological competition or dimension-reduction motivation is not equivalence.
implications_or_equivalences: Do not separately count continuous-time, species-specific, radial-coordinate or extra-convexity variants of this carrying-simplex question.

open_status_evidence_summary: B §6 and MNR §1 independently describe the unresolved interior smoothness gap. Full matching resolution was not located in current author/name/mathematical searches; later results inspected retain additional assumptions, lower regularity, local scope or different dimensions.
independent_status_corroboration: B is authored only by Stephen Baigent; MNR has the disjoint authors Janusz Mierczyński, Lei Niu and Alfonso Ruiz-Herrera. Both discuss the open interior gap. Their later joint papers MB/BM26 are scope checks, not additional independent corroboration.
strongest_known_partial_results_and_gap: Convexity plus the established competitive-diffeomorphism hypotheses gives C1 neat embedding; local smoothness near suitable interior repellers and tangent cones at fixed points are known. General carrying simplices remain only Lipschitz without those additional hypotheses.

issues_found: Generic strongly monotone C1 hypersurface theorems could appear to resolve the interior question indirectly.
Boundary peaks and neat embedding must not be conflated with interior smoothness.
Local conjugacy and tangent cones at fixed points are weaker than smoothness at every interior point.
The map class and matrix numerator must match the formulation source exactly; radial equivalence needs transversality.
issues_resolved: Read BEN standing assumptions and basin theorems, compared M99’s full primary discussion of Tereščák, and checked CONVEX §1’s explicit remaining interior gap.
PEAK Proposition 2.2 places its singularities at axial equilibria; no interior counterexample.
MNR Theorem 4.1 is topological; Corollaries 4.8–4.9 have extra local hypotheses; Theorem 4.12 treats fixed points.

B Theorem 1 was visually checked earlier, including the xi numerator and closed box. Unordered C1 hypersurfaces have nonnegative normals, transverse to strictly positive radial vectors, which justifies the radial formulation.
Repeated local semantic comparison with baseline 154, 190, 283 and 296; none has the same model and regularity conclusion. Corrected the draft heading to the required Applied significance.
